In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''homogeneous variety''' is an [[algebraic variety]] on which an [[algebraic group]] acts transitively.<ref>Michel Brion, "Introduction to actions of algebraic groups" [http://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~mbrion/notes_luminy.pdf], Definition 1.17</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last = Chow |first= Wei-Liang |author-link=Wei-Liang Chow |title = On the projective embedding of homogeneous varieties | journal = Princeton Mathematical Series | volume = 12 | pages = 122-128 | year = 1957}}</ref> Homogeneous varieties over an [[algebraically closed field]] are [[Quotient variety|quotient varieties]] {{math|''G''/''H''}} where {{mvar|G}} is an algebraic group and {{mvar|H}} a [[group scheme|subgroup scheme]] (for instance, an algebraic subgroup).<ref>Michel Brion, "Introduction to actions of algebraic groups" [http://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~mbrion/notes_luminy.pdf], Theorem 1.16</ref>

Such varieties are always [[smooth variety|smooth]] [[quasi-projective varieties]]. 

Classical examples are [[flag varieties]] (when {{mvar|G}} is semisimple and {{mvar|H}} a [[Parabolic subgroups of algebraic groups|parabolic subgroup]]), or more generally homogeneous [[spherical variety|spherical varieties]]. [[Severi–Brauer variety|Severi-Brauer varieties]] are examples of homogeneous varieties over a field without any rational points.
